front.title: MAP Wire Format and Registry Index

abstract.t: This document is the wire-level reference for the MAP (Manolito Agent Protocol) family. It presents the protocol data unit layering — transport frame, signed COSE_Sign1 envelope over deterministic CBOR, protected and body headers, and message-type-selected content — as a single diagram with the field-level detail each layer's owning document specifies, so that an implementer can see the whole encoding in one place. It then consolidates every code point the family assigns: message types, error codes, body and protected-header keys, cryptographic suites, capability-ontology terms, delegation caveats, chunk kinds, settlement methods, pricing models, dispute claim codes, and the remaining registries, each with its registration policy and a pointer to the document that owns it.

This document is an index, not a normative source. Where it disagrees with an owning document, the owning document governs. It defines no protocol behavior of its own and requests no IANA action of its own.

section.name: Requirements Language
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document family are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [RFC2119] [RFC8174] when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here. No adaptation or weakening of these terms applies.

section.name: Purpose and how to read this document
section.t: This document is the consolidated, non-normative index of the MAP wire format and of every assigned registry in the family. It exists so a reader can see the whole on-the-wire picture and the complete code-point space in one place, without opening all eight normative drafts.

It is an index, not a normative source. The normative definitions — CDDL, validation rules, MUST/SHOULD requirements, and the exact bytes — remain in the owning documents listed below. Where this index and an owning document disagree, the owning document wins (engineering policy: one named source of truth per fact, ops §2 rule 1).

section.name: The MAP Protocol Data Unit (PDU) layering
section.t: Every MAP message is a signed CBOR/COSE envelope. The layering, top to bottom:
section.sourcecode: AgentID / key material (identity §3) │ ▼ Envelope = COSE_Sign1 (core §4) [ protected(ProtHdr), payload(Body), signature ] │ ▼ Body = { (core §4.1) version, msg-type, msg-id, timestamp, [recipient], [ttl-ms], [session-id], [seq], [crit], [ext], content } │ ▼ content := selected by msg-type (core §5 registry → owning doc) HELLO / HELLO_ACK / PING / PONG / CLOSE / ERROR / FLOW_CREDIT (core §6, §8, §9) DESCRIPTOR / STATUS_QUERY / STATUS_REPORT / CAP_QUERY / CAP_RESPONSE (discovery §2, §3, §7) OFFER / QUOTE / ASSIGN / ACCEPT / REJECT / CHUNK / TOOL_CALL / TOOL_GRANT / TOOL_RESULT / CHECKPOINT / CHECKPOINT_ACK / CANCEL / COMPLETE / RESUME / RESERVE / LEASE / LEASE_RELEASE (tasks §2–§6, §8, §11) RECEIPT / RECEIPT_ACK / EVIDENCE_QUERY / EVIDENCE_SET / CHALLENGE / CHALLENGE_RESPONSE (trust §2, §4, §8) PAY_QUOTE / PAY_AGREE / PAY_INVOICE / PAY_PROOF / PAY_RECEIPT / PAY_DISPUTE / PAY_DISPUTE_EVIDENCE (pay §2–§6) │ ▼ Task transcript commitment (tasks §8.1) Merkle root over output/tool CHUNKs (kinds 0, 1, 4)
section.t: Two transmission contexts (core §7):

ul.li: In-session: the envelope's COSE external_aad is the channel-binding

section.t: token CB (core §7.3); recipient, session-id, and seq are REQUIRED.
external_aad is empty; ttl-ms is REQUIRED; freshness/supersession rules are per object class (core §7.4).
Four design invariants bind every layer (core §1):

ul.li: I1 — signatures cover the exact transmitted bytes; verifiers MUST NOT

section.t: re-serialize before verifying.

ul.li: I2 — every envelope is independently verifiable from the sender's key

section.t: material alone.

ul.li: I3 — unknown non-critical fields are ignored and preserved verbatim

section.t: when stored or forwarded.

ul.li: I4 — all normative structures are CDDL (RFC 8610) over the deterministic

section.t: CBOR profile (core §4.2; RFC 8949 §4.2.1).

section.name: Master Registry Index
section.t: Each subsection lists the assigned values (copied from the owning document) and a "Defined in" pointer to the normative definition. Registration policy for each registry is in ops §3 (summary in §4 below).

section.name: Cryptographic Suites (core §2)
section.t: Suite 3 is a placeholder; its code point MUST NOT be used until a companion specification defines it. Policy: Standards Action.

section.name: Message Types (core §5)

tr.td: Core: HELLO 0x0001, HELLO_ACK 0x0002, PING 0x0003, PONG 0x0004, CLOSE 0x0005, ERROR 0x0006, FLOW_CREDIT 0x0007
Discovery: DESCRIPTOR 0x0100, STATUS_QUERY 0x0101, STATUS_REPORT 0x0102, CAP_QUERY 0x0103, CAP_RESPONSE 0x0104

Tasks: OFFER 0x0200, QUOTE 0x0201, ASSIGN 0x0202, ACCEPT 0x0203, REJECT 0x0204, CHUNK 0x0205, TOOL_CALL 0x0207, TOOL_GRANT 0x0208, TOOL_RESULT 0x0209, CHECKPOINT 0x020A, CHECKPOINT_ACK 0x020B, CANCEL 0x020C, COMPLETE 0x020D, RESUME 0x020E, RESERVE 0x020F, LEASE 0x0210, LEASE_RELEASE 0x0211
Trust: RECEIPT 0x0300, RECEIPT_ACK 0x0301, EVIDENCE_QUERY 0x0302, EVIDENCE_SET 0x0303, CHALLENGE 0x0304, CHALLENGE_RESPONSE 0x0305
Pay: PAY_QUOTE 0x0400, PAY_AGREE 0x0401, PAY_INVOICE 0x0402, PAY_PROOF 0x0403, PAY_RECEIPT 0x0404, PAY_DISPUTE 0x0405, PAY_DISPUTE_EVIDENCE 0x0406

section.t: 0x0206 is deliberately unassigned (never reused; ops §3.3). Registration policy: Specification Required.

section.name: Body Keys (core §4.1)
section.t: 0 version, 1 msg-type, 2 msg-id, 3 timestamp, 4 recipient, 5 ttl-ms, 6 session-id, 7 seq, 8 crit, 9 ext, 10 content. Key 33 (delegation chain) resides in ProtHdr (core §4.1). Registration policy: Specification Required.

section.name: Extension Keys (core §5.1)
section.t: Points ≥ 0xF000 are private use. Policy: Specification Required.

section.name: Error Codes (core §9)

tr.td: 1000 malformed, 1001 unsupported version/suite, 1002 unknown critical extension, 1003 replay/out-of-window/bad-seq, 1004 message too large, 1005 rate limited / no credit, 1006 state violation
2000 bad signature/identity misbind, 2001 expired object, 2002 revoked key, 2003 invalid delegation chain, 2004 zone violation, 2005 not authorized for message type, 2006 countersignature refused
3000 unsupported message/capability, 3001 model unavailable, 3002 context too large, 3003 ontology term unknown
4000 overloaded, 4001 queue full, 4002 insufficient memory/VRAM class, 4003 reservation expired, 4004 storage exhausted
5000 task failed, 5001 deadline/TTFT exceeded, 5002 cancelled, 5003 checkpoint invalid, 5004 tool denied, 5005 output policy violation, 5006 resumption impossible

6000 quote expired, 6001 payment required, 6002 settlement failed (generic), 6003 dispute opened, 6004 method unsupported, 6005 authorized cap exceeded, 6006 agreement digest mismatch, 6007 task-binding mismatch, 6008 invalid payment proof, 6009 invoice-watermark violation, 6010 escrow violation

section.t: Policy: Specification Required.

section.name: Transport Bindings (core §10)
section.t: libp2p protocol ID /map/1.0.0 (RECOMMENDED); Raw QUIC ALPN map/1; TCP+TLS 1.3 ALPN map/1; WebSocket subprotocol map.v1; gRPC binding (optional, non-normative). Policy: Specification Required.

section.name: AgentID Key Types (identity §11)
section.t: 0xED01 = Ed25519 public key (suite 1/2). Future suites register their multicodec here. Policy: Standards Action.

section.name: Delegation Caveats (identity §4, §11)

tr.td: 32-byte TaskID — chain valid only for envelopes referencing that task
34-byte AgentID — chain valid only when validated by that party

section.t: An unknown caveat key MUST invalidate the chain (fail-closed). Policy: Expert Review.

section.name: Revocation Reasons (identity §11)
section.t: 0 unspecified, 1 compromise, 2 superseded, 3 cessation. Policy: Expert Review.

section.name: Capability Ontology (discovery §4)
section.t: Hierarchical URIs under map:cap: — initial branches: inference/text-generation[/code|/chat], inference/embedding, inference/vision | /speech-to-text | /text-to-speech | /image-gen, tool/git | /shell | /compiler/<lang> | /browser | /sql, lang/<bcp47-or-programming-language-tag>, memory/<domain>, relay, gateway/<namespace>, schedule/reservation. Matching is by exact segment prefix. Policy: Expert Review.

section.name: CapEntry Parameter Keys (discovery §4, §12)

tr.td: tstr namespace — the fronted capability is re-advertised through this gateway namespace

section.t: Policy: Expert Review (immutable once assigned, ops §3.3).

section.name: Hardware / Sandbox Classes (discovery §12)
section.t: HardwareClass: vram-class (0 n/a … 9 >128 GB), ram-class (same scale), accel (0 none … 4 cpu-only), bandwidth-class (1 ≤100Mb … 3 >1Gb). SecurityProfile sandbox: 0 none, 1 container, 2 microVM, 3 wasm, 4 tee. Policy: Expert Review.

section.name: Chunk Kinds (tasks §3)
section.t: 0 output-text, 1 output-bytes, 2 log, 3 usage-update, 4 tool-io. Policy: Expert Review.

section.name: Reservation / Lease Fields (tasks §6)
section.t: Message types RESERVE 0x020F, LEASE 0x0210, LEASE_RELEASE 0x0211; rsv-id is the idempotency key. Policy: Expert Review.

section.name: Task Caveat Keys (tasks §16)
section.t: delegable, budget, args-digest (tool-grant caveats). Policy: Expert Review.

section.name: Receipt Outcome Codes (trust §3)
section.t: 0 ok, 1 failed, 2 timeout, 3 cancelled, 4 disputed. Policy: Expert Review.

section.name: Trust Evidence Query Params / Vouch Caveat Keys / Challenge Modes (trust §11)
section.t: EvidenceQuery fields (subject, scope, window, limit, role filter); vouch records are DelegationCert-shaped; CHALLENGE/CHALLENGE_RESPONSE (0x0304/ 0x0305) for disclosed canary audits. Policy: Expert Review.

section.name: Settlement Methods (pay §5.1)
section.t: Each entry's defining document specifies params, proof, verification, and finality/reversal model. Policy: Specification Required.

section.name: Pricing Models / Terms / Rate-table Unit Codes (pay §3, §8)
section.t: Pricing models: 0 flat, 1 per-token (in/out rates), 2 per-second, 3 per-invocation. Terms: 0 postpaid, 1 prepaid, 2 escrow, 3 metered-incremental. Unit codes: 0 flat total, 1 per token in, 2 per token out, 3 per millisecond, 4 per invocation. Policy: Specification Required.

section.name: Dispute Claim Codes / Evidence-item Kinds (pay §6.1, §8)
section.t: Claim codes: 0 non-delivery, 1 output-mismatch, 2 non-payment, 3 overbilling, 4 terms breach. Evidence-item kinds: 0 PAY_QUOTE envelope, 1 PAY_AGREE, 2 PAY_INVOICE, 3 PAY_PROOF, 4 PAY_RECEIPT, 5 countersigned checkpoint, 6 COMPLETE, 7 ExecutionReceipt, 8 method artifact, 9 CHUNK envelope. Policy: Specification Required.

section.name: Registration policies and change control
section.t: Each registry's IANA policy (from ops §3):

tr.td: Message Types, Body Keys, Error Codes, Extension Keys, Transport Bindings, Settlement Methods, Pricing Models, Terms, Unit Codes, Dispute codes/kinds
Capability Ontology, Delegation Caveats, Chunk Kinds, HW/Sandbox Classes, Revocation Reasons, Task Caveat Keys, CapEntry Parameter Keys, Trust Evidence/Vouch/Challenge

section.t: Immutability (ops §3.3): code points are never reused or redefined; deprecation marks them reserved forever. Deprecation process (ops §3.4): mark deprecated → ≥2 minor versions dual support → remove only at a major version. Private ranges (core §5, ext keys ≥ 0xF000) need no registration and MUST NOT appear in public-mesh descriptors.

section.name: Conformance classes
section.t: MAP-Core (REQUIRED: identity + core); MAP-Discovery; MAP-Tasks; MAP-Trust; MAP-Pay; MAP-Fed (arch §10). A conforming provider/requester implements Core + Discovery + Tasks; Trust and Pay are RECOMMENDED on public meshes.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: This document is a wire-format layering summary and a consolidated registry index; it introduces no mechanism beyond those in the protocol documents, whose security considerations apply unchanged. In particular, all code-point and key registrations indexed here are consumed under the deterministic-CBOR and signed-envelope rules of draft-map-core-01 §4, whose Security Considerations govern malleability, downgrade, and replay.

section.name: IANA Considerations
section.t: This document defines no new registry of its own. It provides a consolidated index (§3) of the registries defined by the MAP protocol documents; each registry's contents, assignment policy, and change control are normative in its defining document, and the registration policies are summarized in §4. No IANA action is requested by this document beyond those already requested by the protocol documents it indexes.

section.name: References (selected)
section.t: [RFC2119] [RFC8174] BCP 14 requirement levels. [RFC8610] CDDL. [RFC8949] CBOR. [RFC9052] COSE. Owning documents: draft-map-core-01, draft-map-identity-01, draft-map-discovery-01, draft-map-tasks-01, draft-map-trust-01, draft-map-pay-01, draft-map-ops-01.
